# Matrix <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Language Features](Language-Features) · [Types](Language-Features-Types)

</div>


```blitzbasic
FloatMatrix2x2(column1, column2)
TypeMatrixCxR(numbers or vectors)
Local m:TypeMatrixCxR
```

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

A matrix is C columns of R numbers of one number type, kept as one value. The name of the type is the number type, `Matrix`, the width, `x` and the height: `FloatMatrix4x3` is 4 columns of `FloatVector3`, `DoubleMatrix2x2` is 2 by 2. Every number type has them, and each size is from 1 to 1024. Like a `Float` it is a value: copying one gives a second one and there is nothing to free.

The type name is also the function that makes one, from numbers, from one number for all of them, or from column vectors; with nothing it is all zeros. `m[1]` is the second column as a vector and `m[1][0]` is one number.

`*` between two matrices is the matrix product, a matrix times a vector multiplies it as a column, and a vector times a matrix as a row. `+ - /`, `Mod` and `^` work number by number, and `=` and `<>` compare all numbers. The rest is on [Vectors and matrices](Vectors-and-Matrices).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Local m:FloatMatrix2x2 = FloatMatrix2x2(FloatVector2(1, 2), FloatVector2(3, 4))
Print m[1][0]
Print m[0][1]
```

```text
3.0
2.0
```
